```{r}
################################################################################
# PHASE 1: ENVIRONMENT SETUP & DATA ACQUISITION
################################################################################

# 1.1 Load Libraries
# Using pacman to ensure all packages are installed and loaded automatically
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse, tidyquant, PerformanceAnalytics, PortfolioAnalytics, 
  ROI, ROI.plugin.quadprog, quadprog, zoo, ggplot2, tidyr, 
  purrr, lubridate, readr, timetk, TTR
)
```

```{r}
# 1.2 Define Tickers and Timeframe
# We use a broad range to cover both the 2022 crash and the 2023 recovery
tickers <- c("SPY", "AGG", "BIL")
start_date <- "2021-01-01"
end_date   <- "2024-01-01"

# 1.3 Download Data
prices <- tq_get(tickers, from = start_date, to = end_date)

# 1.4 Format Data for Portfolio Analysis
# We need "Wide" format (tickers as columns) for the MPT and 60/40 benchmarking later
prices_wide <- prices %>%
  select(date, symbol, adjusted) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = adjusted) %>%
  tk_xts(date_var = date)

returns_wide <- Return.calculate(prices_wide) %>% na.omit()

```


```{r}
# Check the data
print("--- First few rows of Returns Data ---")
head(returns_wide)

print("--- Data Summary ---")
summary(returns_wide)

```


```{r}

################################################################################
# PHASE 2: STRATEGY LOGIC & BASELINE TESTING
################################################################################

# 2.1 Calculate CCI (AI Logic) and SMA (Human Benchmark)
# We focus on SPY for this tactical test
strategy_data <- prices %>%
  filter(symbol == "SPY") %>%
  # Adding CCI - Commodity Channel Index with a 100-period window as optimized in Phase 1
  tq_mutate(select = c(high, low, close), mutate_fun = CCI, n = 100) %>%
  # Adding 50-day SMA - Simple Moving Average as the human benchmark
  tq_mutate(select = adjusted, mutate_fun = SMA, n = 50, col_rename = "sma_50")

# 2.2 Generate Signals
strategy_data <- strategy_data %>%
  mutate(
    # AI Logic: Buy when CCI < -100, Exit when CCI > 100
    ai_raw_signal = case_when(
      cci < -100 ~ 1,
      cci > 100  ~ 0,
      TRUE       ~ NA_real_
    ),
    # Use na.locf to "stay in the trade" until the exit signal is hit
    ai_position = na.locf(ai_raw_signal, na.rm = FALSE) %>% replace_na(0),
    
    # Human Logic: Simple trend following (Buy if Price > SMA)
    sma_position = ifelse(adjusted > sma_50, 1, 0)
  )


# 2.3 Calculate Returns

bil_data <- tq_get("BIL", from = "2021-01-01", to = "2024-01-01") %>%
  tq_transmute(select = adjusted, mutate_fun = periodReturn, period = "daily", col_rename = "bil_ret")

# 2. Join the data and THEN calculate
strategy_results <- strategy_data %>%
  left_join(bil_data, by = "date") %>% # This is the critical alignment step
  mutate(
    daily_ret = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted)),
    # Use your logic from before, now that bil_ret is available in the pipe
    ai_strategy_ret = (lag(ai_position) * daily_ret) + ((1 - lag(ai_position)) * bil_ret),
    human_sma_ret   = (lag(sma_position) * daily_ret) + ((1 - lag(sma_position)) * bil_ret)
  ) %>% 
  na.omit()

```

```{r}
################################################################################
# PHASE 3: MODERN PORTFOLIO THEORY & OPTIMIZATION
################################################################################

# 3.1 Dynamic Mean-Variance Optimization Function

optimize_mpt_weights <- function(R_data) {
  # Logic: Use expected return (mu) and covariance (sigma) (Req 2)
  mu <- colMeans(R_data[, c("SPY", "AGG", "BIL")])
  sigma <- cov(R_data[, c("SPY", "AGG", "BIL")])
  n <- length(mu)
  
  # NEW: Dynamic target return based on 60/40 benchmark (Req 2)
  w_bench <- c(0.60, 0.40, 0.00)
  target_ret <- sum(mu * w_bench) 
  
  # Quadprog Solver Setup
  Dmat <- sigma
  dvec <- rep(0, n)
  Amat <- cbind(rep(1, n), mu, diag(n))
  bvec <- c(1, target_ret, rep(0, n))
  
  opt <- solve.QP(Dmat, dvec, Amat, bvec, meq = 2)
  weights <- opt$solution
  names(weights) <- names(mu)
  return(weights)
}

mpt_weights <- optimize_mpt_weights(returns_wide)

# 3.2 Define Benchmarks (Requirement 3)
benchmark_weights <- c(SPY = 0.60, AGG = 0.40)

```


```{r}
################################################################################
# PHASE 4: THE REBALANCING ENGINE & MULTI-FREQUENCY TESTING
################################################################################

# 4.1 Execution Rules (Requirement 8)
t_cost <- 0.001 # 10bps slippage/commissions 
returns_xts <- as.xts(returns_wide[, c("SPY", "AGG", "BIL")])

# 4.2 Multi-Frequency Rebalancing (Requirement 1)
frequencies <- c("months", "quarters")
all_rebalance_results <- list()

#4.3 Weight Alignment & XTS Formatting

# We repeat the optimized mpt_weights for every observation in the returns index
weight_matrix <- matrix(
  rep(mpt_weights, length(index(returns_xts))), 
  nrow = length(index(returns_xts)), 
  ncol = 3, 
  byrow = TRUE
)

# Convert to xts to satisfy the Return.portfolio requirements
mpt_weights_xts <- xts(weight_matrix, order.by = index(returns_xts))
colnames(mpt_weights_xts) <- c("SPY", "AGG", "BIL")

# 4.4 Execution Loop with Dynamic Friction
for(freq in frequencies) {
  
  # Apply Portfolio Construction (Requirement 4)
  # Using verbose = TRUE is critical to extract BOP/EOP weights for turnover
  mpt_port_obj <- Return.portfolio(
    R = returns_xts, 
    weights = mpt_weights_xts, 
    rebalance_on = freq, 
    geometric = TRUE,
    verbose = TRUE
  )
  
  # Extract Gross Returns
  gross_returns <- mpt_port_obj$returns
  
  # Calculate Turnover-Based Friction (Requirement 8)
  # We calculate the absolute change in weights at each period to apply the 10bpscost
  # This avoids the "static cost" error and matches the R-backtesting framework
  turnover <- rowSums(abs(mpt_port_obj$BOP.Weight - lag(mpt_port_obj$EOP.Weight)), na.rm = TRUE)
  
# Net Return = Gross Return - (Turnover * Transaction Cost)
  net_mpt <- gross_returns - (turnover * t_cost)
  
  # Store results in the list
  all_rebalance_results[[paste0("MPT_", freq)]] <- net_mpt
}

# 4.5 Performance Consolidation
# Merging all frequency results into a single object for Phase 5 Ranking
portfolio_comparison <- do.call(merge, all_rebalance_results)
colnames(portfolio_comparison) <- c("MPT_Monthly", "MPT_Quarterly")

# Review the first few rows of net performance
head(portfolio_comparison)

```

```{r}
################################################################################
# PHASE 5: AI STRATEGY ITERATION LOOP & FINAL COMPARISON
################################################################################

# 5.1 Define the AI Strategy Variants
# This allows for easy adaptation of different prompts or lookback periods
ai_variants <- list(
  "AI_Aggressive"   = list(n = 20,  thresh = 100),
  "AI_Standard"     = list(n = 100, thresh = 100),
  "AI_Conservative" = list(n = 200, thresh = 150)
)

# 5.2 The Iteration Loop
# We use a loop to backtest each variant and save the results for ranking
ai_iteration_results <- list()

# Re-isolating HLC data for the loop to ensure clean calculation
spy_hlc <- prices %>% 
  filter(symbol == "SPY") %>% 
  select(high, low, close)

for(name in names(ai_variants)) {
  params <- ai_variants[[name]]
  
  # Calculate CCI as a numeric vector using the TTR package
  cci_vec <- as.numeric(TTR::CCI(spy_hlc, n = params$n))
  
  # Signal Logic: Buy (1) when oversold, Exit (0) when overbought
  sig <- case_when(
    cci_vec < -params$thresh ~ 1,
    cci_vec > params$thresh  ~ 0,
    TRUE                     ~ NA_real_
  )
  
  # Forward fill (Requirement 4) to "stay in the trade"
  pos <- na.locf(sig, na.rm = FALSE)
  pos[is.na(pos)] <- 0
  pos_xts <- xts(pos, order.by = index(prices_wide))
  
  # Inside the Phase 5.2 loop
  trades <- abs(pos_xts - Lag(pos_xts))
  trades[1] <- 0 # Initialize first row
  cost_penalty <- trades * t_cost
  
  # Calculate returns: Lagged Position * SPY Returns
  # We use 'setNames' to ensure the column name matches the variant name
  
  strat_ret_net <- (Lag(pos_xts) * returns_xts[,"SPY"]) + ((1 - Lag(pos_xts)) * returns_xts[,"BIL"]) - Lag(cost_penalty)
  strat_ret_net[1] <- 0 
  strat_ret <- setNames(strat_ret_net, name)
   
  
  ai_iteration_results[[name]] <- na.omit(strat_ret)
}

# 5.3 Merge AI Results
final_ai_merged <- do.call(merge, ai_iteration_results)

# 5.4 Merge with Professional Benchmark (MPT from Phase 4)
# This fulfills the requirement to compare against a 60/40 benchmark
final_comparison_all <- merge(final_ai_merged, portfolio_comparison$MPT_Monthly)

# FIX: Dynamic naming to avoid 'dimnames' error
names_from_loop <- names(ai_iteration_results)
all_col_names <- c(names_from_loop, "MPT_Monthly")

if(ncol(final_comparison_all) == length(all_col_names)) {
  colnames(final_comparison_all) <- all_col_names
}

# 5.5 Final Performance Ranking (Requirement 7)
print("--- FINAL STRATEGY RANKING (2021-2024) ---")

# 1. Generate the standard returns table
stats_table <- table.AnnualizedReturns(na.omit(final_comparison_all))

# 2. Generate the Max Drawdown row specifically
# we use na.omit to ensure the calculation is clean
mdd_row <- maxDrawdown(na.omit(final_comparison_all))

# 3. Combine them: rbind "glues" the new row to the bottom
# We also give the new row a clean name
rownames(mdd_row) <- "Max Drawdown"
combined_results <- rbind(stats_table, mdd_row)

# 4. Extract the Sharpe Ratio row (row 3) for the ranking logic
sharpe_ratios <- as.numeric(stats_table[3, ])

# 5. Reorder the columns of our NEW combined table based on those Sharpes
ranked_stats <- combined_results[, order(sharpe_ratios, decreasing = TRUE)]

# Now when you print, the 4th row will be Max Drawdown
print(ranked_stats)

# 5.6 Visual Comparison

# Adjust margins to make room for labels (bottom, left, top, right)
par(mar = c(8.2, 6, 4, 2))

#Run plot with labels
chart.CumReturns(na.omit(final_comparison_all), 
                 main = "Final Outcome: Tactical AI Variants vs. Diversified MPT",
                 legend.loc = "topleft", 
                 colorset = rich8equal)

title(xlab = "Time Period (2021-2024)", line = 6, cex.lab = 1.2)
title(ylab = "Cumulative Log Returns", line = 4.7, cex.lab =1.2)
                

```

```{r}
################################################################################
# PHASE 6: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS - TRIGGER-BASED WEEKLY MONITORING
################################################################################


# 6.1 Define a 5% Tolerance Band (The "Threshold")
# This addresses the professor's point: We monitor weekly, but only trade if 
# an asset drifts by more than 5% from its target weight.
threshold <- 0.05

# 6.2 Execute Weekly Monitoring Logic
mpt_weekly_obj <- Return.portfolio(
  R = returns_xts, 
  weights = mpt_weights_xts, 
  rebalance_on = "weeks", # Monitor weekly
  geometric = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# 6.3 Calculate "Smart" Turnover
drift_raw <- mpt_weekly_obj$BOP.Weight - lag(mpt_weekly_obj$EOP.Weight)
actual_drift <- na.omit(abs(drift_raw))

# Convert to coredata for the logical check to avoid indexing errors
# We check if the drift of ANY asset exceeds the 5% threshold
drift_matrix <- coredata(actual_drift)
smart_turnover_matrix <- ifelse(drift_matrix > threshold, drift_matrix, 0)

# Condense into a single total turnover value per period
total_smart_turnover <- rowSums(smart_turnover_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)

# Re-align as an xts object using the indices from actual_drift
total_smart_turnover_xts <- xts(total_smart_turnover, order.by = index(actual_drift))

# 6.4 Calculate Net Performance
# Subset the returns to match the dates where we have turnover data
aligned_returns <- mpt_weekly_obj$returns[index(total_smart_turnover_xts)]
net_mpt_weekly <- aligned_returns - (total_smart_turnover_xts * t_cost)
colnames(net_mpt_weekly) <- "MPT_Weekly_Threshold"

# 6.5 Final Sensitivity Comparison
# We merge with na.omit to ensure all compared strategies share the same timeframe
sensitivity_results <- table.AnnualizedReturns(na.omit(merge(portfolio_comparison, net_mpt_weekly)))
print("--- REBALANCING SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS ---")
print(sensitivity_results)
```
